200.title: OK
200.description: The request succeeded and the server returned the requested resource or operation result.
200.serverAdminConcern: Low — Healthy response indicating IIS and the application pipeline completed normally.
200.applicationSupportConcern: Low — Baseline success status used for normal request handling.
likelyCauses: Request matched a valid route, handler, or static file
No upstream timeout or dependency failure occurred
checks: If unexpected, verify client cache-control headers and request URL
Review application logs to confirm expected business behavior
Use W3C fields sc-status, sc-substatus, time-taken for performance analysis

304.title: Not Modified
304.description: The resource has not changed since the client's last request, so no response body is sent.
304.serverAdminConcern: Low — Expected cache validation behavior that reduces bandwidth and server load.
304.applicationSupportConcern: Low — Indicates conditional request headers were processed correctly.
likelyCauses: Client sent If-None-Match with a matching ETag
Client sent If-Modified-Since and the resource timestamp has not changed
Static file or proxy cache validation is working as intended
checks: Confirm Cache-Control, ETag, and Last-Modified headers are configured as expected
If unexpected, compare response headers between 200 and 304 flows
Verify proxies/CDNs are not overriding caching policy

400.title: Bad Request
400.description: The server cannot process the request because the client sent malformed syntax, invalid headers, oversized fields, or content that violates rules.
400.serverAdminConcern: Low — Usually traceable to a single bad client, proxy, or integration unless spikes indicate abuse.
400.applicationSupportConcern: Medium — Often indicates invalid API usage, serialization bugs, or schema mismatches in app code.
likelyCauses: Malformed HTTP request line, headers, or cookie values
Body encoding or JSON/XML that fails parsing or validation
URL or header length limits exceeded
WAF or reverse proxy rewriting requests incorrectly
checks: Capture the raw request (Fiddler, browser dev tools, Postman) and compare with API documentation
Review application validation and model binding errors in logs
Check IIS Failed Request Tracing or ASP.NET detailed errors for the failing module
Verify load balancer or firewall is not stripping or corrupting headers

401.title: Unauthorized
401.description: Authentication is required or credentials were rejected before the request could be authorized.
401.serverAdminConcern: Medium — Often IIS authentication configuration, certificates, or domain/Kerberos issues.
401.applicationSupportConcern: Medium — App-level login, tokens, API keys, or identity provider integration problems.
likelyCauses: Anonymous authentication disabled when clients expect it
checks: Confirm which authentication methods are enabled on the site and app pool identity
Review IIS logs fields c-ip, cs-username, sc-substatus for specific 401.x meaning
Test with a known-good account and compare with failing users
Validate clocks (Kerberos), SSL certificates, and trust between servers

403.title: Forbidden
403.description: The server understood the request but refuses to fulfill it; credentials may be valid but authorization or policy denies access.
403.serverAdminConcern: Medium — NTFS ACLs, IP restrictions, SSL policies, or site bindings.
403.applicationSupportConcern: Medium — Role-based rules, URL authorization, or business logic denying access.
likelyCauses: Insufficient NTFS permissions on content or scripts
URL Authorization rules denying users or verbs
Client certificate or SSL requirements not met
checks: Compare app pool identity vs folder ACLs on physical paths
Inspect URL Authorization and Request Filtering rules
Check IP restriction modules and reverse proxy forwarded headers
Verify SSL bindings and whether anonymous vs authenticated users are expected

404.title: Not Found
404.description: No resource matched the requested URL, or an IIS rule hid or blocked the mapping before your application ran.
404.serverAdminConcern: Low — Unless widespread, often content deployment or virtual directory issues.
404.applicationSupportConcern: Medium — Wrong routes, missing static files, or API versioning mismatches.
likelyCauses: Typo in URL, missing file after deployment
Incorrect application path or virtual directory
Handler mapping or rewrite rule sending traffic elsewhere
ASP.NET routing not registering expected endpoints
checks: Confirm physical file exists under the site root the app pool can read
Review Failed Request Tracing and Failed Request logs for rewrite outcomes
Check web.config for handlers, default documents, and aspNetCore hosting paths
For SPA apps, ensure fallback routing or static file middleware is configured

408.title: Request Timeout
408.description: The server gave up waiting for the complete request from the client within the allowed time.
408.serverAdminConcern: Low to Medium — May indicate slow networks, large uploads, or aggressive timeouts.
408.applicationSupportConcern: Low — Unless app holds connections open during long server-side work.
likelyCauses: Timeouts set too low on IIS, reverse proxy, or firewall
checks: Increase request timeouts where large uploads are expected
Inspect intermediate proxies (ARR, nginx, Application Gateway) timeout settings
Correlate with client-side logs and network captures

413.title: Payload Too Large
413.description: The request body exceeds limits configured on IIS, ASP.NET, or an upstream proxy.
413.serverAdminConcern: Medium — Requires raising limits consistently across IIS and proxies.
413.applicationSupportConcern: Medium — Design uploads to chunk or stream within limits.
likelyCauses: ASP.NET Core Kestrel/IIS max body limits
checks: Raise maxAllowedContentLength in web.config requestFiltering
Adjust ASP.NET Core server limits and multipart boundaries
Align Azure Front Door, nginx, or ARR upload limits with IIS

429.title: Too Many Requests
429.description: The client exceeded a configured rate limit or throttling policy.
429.serverAdminConcern: Medium — Capacity, DDoS mitigation, or reverse proxy rate limits.
429.applicationSupportConcern: Medium — Client retry storms or missing backoff.
checks: Identify the component emitting 429 (app vs gateway)
Review Retry-After headers and client backoff logic
Tune limits or scale out if legitimate traffic is throttled

500.title: Internal Server Error
500.description: An unexpected failure occurred while processing the request; use IIS substatus (500.x) when logged to pinpoint modules or configuration.
500.serverAdminConcern: High — Misconfiguration, failing modules, or unstable worker processes.
500.applicationSupportConcern: High — Unhandled exceptions, dependency outages, or corrupt application state.
likelyCauses: Unhandled exceptions in managed or native code
Out of memory or access violations in worker process
checks: Open Event Viewer Application and System logs for WAS and ASP.NET Core entries
Enable stdout logging for ASP.NET Core under logs folder
Temporarily enable detailed errors only in controlled environments
Collect memory dumps if the worker process recycles frequently

501.title: Not Implemented
501.description: The server does not support the functionality required to fulfill the request (for example an unsupported HTTP method).
501.serverAdminConcern: Low — Rare on IIS unless handlers misconfigured.
501.applicationSupportConcern: Medium — Client calling wrong verb or endpoint.
likelyCauses: DELETE/PUT blocked by handler or WebDAV settings
checks: Verify allowed verbs on handler mappings
Confirm API expects the HTTP method used by the client

502.title: Bad Gateway
502.description: IIS or a reverse proxy acting as gateway received an invalid response from an upstream server.
502.serverAdminConcern: High — ARR, proxy, or backend connectivity issues.
502.applicationSupportConcern: Medium — Backend API unstable or returning malformed responses.
likelyCauses: Upstream application offline or TCP reset
SSL handshake failure between proxy and origin
ARR health probe marking server unhealthy
checks: Verify upstream URL, ports, and certificates from the proxy machine
Review ARR proxy logs and WinHTTP traces
Test origin directly bypassing the gateway
Check firewall rules between tier hosts

503.title: Service Unavailable
503.description: The server cannot handle the request right now—often application pool stopped, recycling, queue limits, or infrastructure saturation.
503.serverAdminConcern: High — Availability and capacity of IIS app pools and dependent services.
503.applicationSupportConcern: Medium to High — Startup failures, deadlock, or dependency outages causing pool stops.
likelyCauses: Application pool stopped or rapid recycling
HTTP.sys queue or ASP.NET queue exhaustion
ARR routing with no healthy servers
checks: Check application pool state and rapid-fail protection settings
Review HTTPERR logs under System32\LogFiles\HTTPERR
Inspect CPU/memory limits on app pools
Validate HTTP.sys URL reservations if multiple sites share bindings
Look at substatus (503.2, 503.3, etc.) in IIS logs when present

504.title: Gateway Timeout
504.description: A gateway or proxy did not receive a timely response from an upstream server.
504.serverAdminConcern: High — Proxy timeouts shorter than backend processing time.
504.applicationSupportConcern: High — Slow queries, remote calls, or missing async timeouts.
likelyCauses: Database or external API latency spikes
Proxy idle/read timeout shorter than backend SLA
checks: Increase gateway timeout or optimize backend latency
Profile slow dependencies with APM or traces
Align ARR/WebSocket/proxy timeouts with realistic worst-case duration

200.0.title: 200.0 - OK
200.0.description: Standard IIS log success status. The request completed successfully with no special substatus condition.
likelyCauses: The request was processed successfully end-to-end
No IIS module, authentication, or authorization error occurred
No application exception interrupted response generation
checks: Treat as healthy baseline traffic
If performance is poor, review time-taken and downstream dependency metrics
Correlate with business logs if users still report issues

304.0.title: 304.0 - Not Modified
304.0.description: Standard IIS cache-validation success status. Resource unchanged, so body is omitted.
304.0.serverAdminConcern: Low — Common and desirable for cacheable content.
304.0.applicationSupportConcern: Low — Indicates conditional GET handling is functioning.
likelyCauses: Matching ETag in If-None-Match request header
Browser or proxy revalidation of cached content
checks: Verify cache headers (ETag, Last-Modified, Cache-Control) align with policy
If content should have changed, confirm deployment invalidated caches correctly
Check CDN/proxy cache behavior for stale metadata

400.0.title: 400.0 - Bad Request
400.0.description: IIS received a malformed request and rejected it with no special substatus condition.
400.0.serverAdminConcern: Low — Usually isolated to specific clients, bots, or integrations.
400.0.applicationSupportConcern: Medium — Can indicate API contract or serialization issues.
likelyCauses: Malformed URL, headers, cookies, or payload
Client or proxy sending invalid HTTP syntax
Request filtering rules rejecting malformed input
checks: Capture the raw request and compare with API expectations
Review IIS and application logs for repeat client patterns
Inspect reverse proxy/WAF rewriting behavior

401.0.title: 401.0 - Unauthorized
401.0.description: Authentication failed or missing credentials with no more specific IIS 401.x detail recorded.
401.0.serverAdminConcern: Medium — Authentication provider/configuration may be mismatched.
401.0.applicationSupportConcern: Medium — Client credentials or token flow may be incorrect.
likelyCauses: Missing Authorization header or expired credentials
Identity provider or domain trust issue
checks: Verify enabled IIS authentication modes for the site
Test with known-good credentials and compare behavior
Correlate with 401.1/401.2/401.3 events if present

403.0.title: 403.0 - Forbidden
403.0.description: IIS denied access with no more specific 403.x substatus provided.
403.0.serverAdminConcern: Medium — Permissions, policy, or filtering may deny valid requests.
403.0.applicationSupportConcern: Medium — Authorization rules may be too restrictive.
likelyCauses: NTFS ACL or URL authorization deny rule
Request filtering or IP restriction policy
checks: Review URL authorization and request filtering configuration
Check site folder permissions for app pool identity
Verify binding/certificate requirements match client access pattern

404.0.title: 404.0 - Not Found
404.0.description: Requested resource was not found with no more specific IIS 404.x classification.
404.0.serverAdminConcern: Low — Common in normal traffic, but spikes can indicate deployment or routing issues.
404.0.applicationSupportConcern: Medium — Route, content path, or version mismatch likely.
likelyCauses: Incorrect virtual directory or rewrite target
Client requesting wrong path or API version
checks: Confirm physical file or route exists on target site
Review rewrite/redirect rules and SPA fallback behavior
Correlate with deployment changes and recently moved content

408.0.title: 408.0 - Request Timeout
408.0.description: Client did not complete the request in time and IIS/HTTP.sys timed out the request.
408.0.serverAdminConcern: Low to Medium — Usually client or network behavior unless sustained.
408.0.applicationSupportConcern: Low — Often external to app logic.
likelyCauses: Timeout values too aggressive for workload
checks: Review client and proxy timeout settings end-to-end
Inspect network path for intermittent packet loss
Tune upload/request timeout thresholds when appropriate

413.0.title: 413.0 - Payload Too Large
413.0.description: Request body exceeded configured limits with no additional IIS-specific substatus.
413.0.serverAdminConcern: Medium — Size limits likely misaligned across IIS/app/proxy.
413.0.applicationSupportConcern: Medium — Client may need chunking/compression or limit guidance.
likelyCauses: Proxy/CDN upload limit lower than IIS
checks: Align payload limits across IIS, app runtime, and proxies
Validate upload scenario with representative file sizes
Consider chunked uploads for large payload workflows

429.0.title: 429.0 - Too Many Requests
429.0.description: Request was throttled due to rate limiting with no additional substatus detail.
429.0.serverAdminConcern: Medium — Throttling may indicate abuse, mis-tuned limits, or traffic bursts.
429.0.applicationSupportConcern: Medium — Clients should use backoff and retry guidance.
likelyCauses: Rate-limiting policy triggered in IIS, proxy, or gateway
Burst traffic from polling clients or automation
checks: Identify which component emitted 429 responses
Review Retry-After handling in clients
Tune limits if legitimate traffic is being throttled

501.0.title: 501.0 - Not Implemented
501.0.description: Requested method or feature is not implemented/allowed, with no specific IIS 501.x detail.
501.0.serverAdminConcern: Low — Often handler mapping or verb support issue.
501.0.applicationSupportConcern: Medium — Client likely using unsupported HTTP method.
checks: Review handler mappings and allowed verbs
Confirm client method matches API contract
Disable conflicting modules if they intercept the route

502.0.title: 502.0 - Bad Gateway
502.0.description: Gateway/proxy chain returned an invalid upstream response with no specific 502.x detail.
502.0.serverAdminConcern: High — Upstream connectivity or proxy behavior needs review.
502.0.applicationSupportConcern: Medium — Backend app may be unstable or unreachable.
likelyCauses: Upstream server reset or malformed response
checks: Test upstream endpoint directly from proxy host
Inspect ARR/reverse proxy logs for upstream errors
Validate TLS bindings and trust between tiers

503.0.title: 503.0 - Service Unavailable
503.0.description: Service was unavailable with no additional IIS 503.x substatus detail.
503.0.serverAdminConcern: High — App pool availability/capacity issue likely.
503.0.applicationSupportConcern: Medium to High — Startup faults or dependency outages may surface as 503.
likelyCauses: Maintenance mode or no healthy upstream targets
checks: Check current app pool state and recent recycles
Review HTTPERR logs for Timer_AppPool/Rejected/QueueFull
Validate health checks and upstream availability

504.0.title: 504.0 - Gateway Timeout
504.0.description: Proxy/gateway timed out waiting for upstream response with no extra IIS-specific detail.
504.0.serverAdminConcern: High — Timeout policy or backend latency mismatch.
504.0.applicationSupportConcern: High — Slow dependencies or long-running requests likely.
likelyCauses: Slow database or external service calls
checks: Compare gateway timeout values with backend response profiles
Profile slow endpoints and dependency calls
Tune timeout values only after confirming root latency causes

401.1.title: 401.1 - Logon failed
401.1.description: IIS rejected the supplied credentials during authentication before authorization ran.
401.1.serverAdminConcern: Medium — Authentication scheme or provider misconfiguration.
401.1.applicationSupportConcern: Medium — Wrong password, locked account, or wrong identity provider.
likelyCauses: Invalid username or password for basic or Windows auth
Domain trust or DC connectivity problems
checks: Verify authentication providers enabled on the site
Test interactive logon or LDAP bind outside IIS
Compare failing accounts against successful ones

401.2.title: 401.2 - Logon failed due to server configuration
401.2.description: Credentials might be fine but IIS authentication configuration prevents logon (scheme mismatch).
401.2.serverAdminConcern: Medium — IIS authentication settings vs client capabilities.
401.2.applicationSupportConcern: Low — Client not sending expected scheme (Negotiate vs NTLM vs Basic).
likelyCauses: Client offers only NTLM but site requires Negotiate
checks: Align authentication modes between IIS, browsers, and reverse proxies
Ensure kernel-mode vs managed authentication settings match expectations
Review AuthPersistSingleRequestPerSession-related settings if cookies involved

401.3.title: 401.3 - Unauthorized due to ACL on resource
401.3.description: Authentication succeeded at IIS but NTFS ACLs deny the authenticated principal.
401.3.serverAdminConcern: High — File system permissions on site content.
401.3.applicationSupportConcern: Low — Unless impersonation changes effective user.
likelyCauses: App pool identity lacks read/execute on physical path
checks: Grant app pool identity read and execute on site root and scripts
Verify impersonation settings if accessing remote UNC shares
Use icacls or Effective Access tab for problematic accounts

401.16.title: 401.16 - Unauthorized (MSDN unspecified)
401.16.description: Often logged when authorization middleware rejects access before the site serves content (specific products map extra meanings—check product docs).
401.16.serverAdminConcern: Medium — Depends on modules installed (URL auth, ARR, etc.).
401.16.applicationSupportConcern: Medium — Match logs to module pipeline order.
checks: Enable Failed Request Tracing to see which module returned 401
Review ordered modules in IIS Manager
Correlate with application authorization policies

403.4.title: 403.4 - SSL required
403.4.description: The resource must be accessed over HTTPS but the request used HTTP.
403.4.serverAdminConcern: Medium — Require SSL flag on site/folder and binding coverage.
403.4.applicationSupportConcern: Low — Hard-coded http links or HSTS misconfiguration.
likelyCauses: Require SSL checkbox enabled without redirect rule
checks: Add HTTPS binding and valid certificate
Implement HTTP to HTTPS redirect at IIS or reverse proxy
Ensure monitoring uses https URLs

403.14.title: 403.14 - Directory listing denied
403.14.description: No default document exists and directory browsing is disabled.
403.14.applicationSupportConcern: Medium — Missing default file or SPA fallback.
likelyCauses: SPA deep links without rewrite to index
checks: Add default document or enable directory browsing only if intentional
Configure URL rewrite for SPA frameworks
Verify publish profile includes root files

404.3.title: 404.3 - MIME map policy
404.3.description: The file extension is blocked because MIME types or handler mappings disallow it.
404.3.serverAdminConcern: Medium — Request filtering staticFile deny extensions.
likelyCauses: Extension not listed in MIME types
checks: Add MIME type or handler for the extension
Remove unintended deny rules from requestFiltering
Confirm static content feature installed

404.13.title: 404.13 - Content length too large
404.13.description: The request body exceeds configured limits before reaching the application.
404.13.serverAdminConcern: Medium — Raise IIS and proxy limits consistently.
404.13.applicationSupportConcern: Medium — Chunk uploads or compress payloads.
checks: Increase limits in web.config requestFiltering
Adjust ASP.NET Core server limits
Verify CDN or WAF upload caps

500.0.title: 500.0 - Module or ISAPI error
500.0.description: An ISAPI extension, CGI, FastCGI module, or HTTP module threw an unhandled error.
500.0.serverAdminConcern: Medium — Faulty native modules or misconfigured handlers.
500.0.applicationSupportConcern: High — Managed exceptions bubbling without handling.
checks: Review Windows Event Log for WAS warnings
Enable Failed Request Tracing with verbose errors in controlled environments
Upgrade faulty modules or capture crash dumps

500.11.title: 500.11 - Application shutting down on the web server
500.11.description: ASP.NET detected the app domain is unloading—often due to configuration change or fatal error.
500.11.serverAdminConcern: Medium — Frequent app domain restarts hurt availability.
500.11.applicationSupportConcern: High — Startup exception or file change churn.
likelyCauses: Bin folder updates during peak traffic
checks: Review ASP.NET Health Monitoring or ETW traces
Stabilize deployments to reduce bin churn
Inspect antivirus locking DLLs in bin

500.12.title: 500.12 - Application is busy restarting
500.12.description: Requests arrived while the application was restarting after a configuration or file change.
500.12.applicationSupportConcern: Medium — Excessive restarts due to file watchers.
checks: Use drain-stop or maintenance pages during deploys
Reduce accidental writes under application folders

500.13.title: 500.13 - Web server is too busy
500.13.description: ASP.NET rejected work because internal queues were full—severe load or deadlock.
500.13.applicationSupportConcern: High — Thread pool starvation or blocking calls.
likelyCauses: Too few worker threads vs synchronous IO
checks: Scale out or increase resources
Convert blocking calls to async
Tune processModel and queue limits carefully with measurement

500.19.title: 500.19 - Internal Server Error - Configuration invalid
500.19.description: IIS failed to read configuration—typically malformed web.config, locked sections, or missing modules.
500.19.serverAdminConcern: High — Deployment or permission issue preventing config load.
500.19.applicationSupportConcern: Medium — Invalid XML or unsupported settings for target framework.
likelyCauses: Missing ASP.NET Core Hosting Bundle / module
Unlock required sections at machine level
Cannot read web.config due to ACL
checks: Validate web.config against schema and framework version
Install correct Hosting Bundle version matching runtime
Run appcmd unlock config or fix ACLs on web.config
Read error detail line/column shown in browser when detailed errors enabled

500.21.title: 500.21 - Internal Server Error - Handler mismatch
500.21.description: A module failed to execute—often handler order issues or bitness mismatch.
500.21.serverAdminConcern: Medium — Handler mappings or modules corrupted.
checks: Reinstall ASP.NET via aspnet_regiis if classic ASP.NET
Verify Enable 32-Bit Applications matches binaries
Repair IIS Express or hosting bundle

500.22.title: 500.22 - ANCM duplicate aspNetCore section
500.22.description: ASP.NET Core ANCM found duplicate aspNetCore configuration sections.
500.22.applicationSupportConcern: Low — Merge duplicate entries from transforms.
checks: Search all web.config files for aspNetCore duplicates
Clean publish output and redeploy

500.23.title: 500.23 - ANCM app offline
500.23.description: ANCM detected app_offline.htm and stopped serving the application.
likelyCauses: Automated deploy script failed to remove offline page
checks: Remove app_offline.htm after maintenance
Automate cleanup in deployment pipeline

500.30.title: 500.30 - In-process start failure
500.30.description: ASP.NET Core Module (ANCM) could not start the app when using the in-process hosting model.
500.30.serverAdminConcern: Medium — Runtime, permissions, or bitness on the server.
500.30.applicationSupportConcern: High — Startup exceptions, missing dependencies, or wrong environment.
likelyCauses: Cannot load native dependencies or certificates
checks: Enable stdout logging in web.config aspNetCore stdoutLogEnabled true
Review Application Event Log for ANCM entries with HRESULT
Match installed Hosting Bundle with app's target framework
Run dotnet your.dll from the publish folder under the app pool identity
Verify working directory and content root paths

500.31.title: 500.31 - Failed to load ASP.NET Core runtime
500.31.description: ANCM could not locate or load the ASP.NET Core shared runtime or app assembly.
500.31.serverAdminConcern: High — Hosting Bundle incomplete or wrong architecture.
checks: dotnet --list-runtimes on the server
Install matching ASP.NET Core Hosting Bundle
Consider self-contained publish if servers cannot be patched quickly

500.32.title: 500.32 - Failed to load aspnetcorev2_inprocess.dll
500.32.description: The native ANCM in-process shim failed to load—often missing hosting bundle files.
checks: Reinstall latest Hosting Bundle
Verify aspnetcorev2.dll exists under Program Files\IIS\Asp.Net Core Module\V2
Match app pool 32-bit flag with installation

500.33.title: 500.33 - In-process ANCM wrong bitness
500.33.description: The worker process architecture does not match the published application binaries.
500.33.serverAdminConcern: Low — Toggle Enable 32-Bit Applications on app pool.
likelyCauses: Arm vs x64 mismatch on specialized hosts
checks: Align app pool bitness with publish output
Republish with correct runtime identifier

500.34.title: 500.34 - In-process ANCM app startup failure
500.34.description: Startup reached Main but hosting shut down due to startup filters or host builder errors.
500.34.serverAdminConcern: Low — Unless policy blocks Kestrel endpoints.
checks: Enable detailed exceptions locally
Validate appsettings.* for target environment
Inspect ANCM stdout logs

500.35.title: 500.35 - ANCM duplicate hosting models
500.35.description: Both in-process and out-of-process hosting settings conflict.
checks: Ensure single aspNetCore element with one hostingModel
Review nested site web.config inheritance

500.36.title: 500.36 - ANCM configuration mismatch
500.36.description: Mismatch between server hosting bundle capabilities and application declared runtime.
500.36.applicationSupportConcern: Medium — Target newer runtime than deployed.
likelyCauses: Preview runtime referenced but not installed
checks: Align TargetFramework with installed shared frameworks
Update global.json rollForward settings intentionally

500.37.title: 500.37 - Startup exceeded time limit
500.37.description: ANCM terminated startup because the app did not become ready in time.
500.37.serverAdminConcern: Medium — Increase startupTimeLimit if cold start is legitimately slow.
likelyCauses: Large DI graphs or synchronous network calls
checks: Increase startupTimeLimit in aspNetCore settings cautiously
Profile startup with logging timestamps
Move heavy work out of synchronous startup path

500.38.title: 500.38 - Hosting model not supported
500.38.description: The chosen hosting model cannot run on this IIS configuration.
500.38.serverAdminConcern: Medium — Wrong IIS modules or OS SKUs.
checks: Switch hostingModel to match supported scenario
Upgrade IIS / Hosting Bundle

502.3.title: 502.3 - Bad Gateway - Forward connection failure
502.3.description: Application Request Routing or WebSocket proxy failed to connect to the defined backend server.
502.3.serverAdminConcern: High — Network path, DNS, or backend offline.
likelyCauses: Backend IP/port wrong in ARR server farm
TLS mismatch or certificate name mismatch
checks: Test Telnet/curl from IIS box to backend URL
Verify ARR health tests and server affinity
Inspect SSL settings for server name indication

502.4.title: 502.4 - Bad Gateway - SSL handshake failed
502.4.description: ARR could not complete TLS with the origin server.
502.4.serverAdminConcern: High — Certificates, protocols, or cipher mismatch.
502.4.applicationSupportConcern: Low — Unless backend uses custom TLS.
likelyCauses: TLS 1.0 disabled but backend requires it
checks: Validate cert chain on IIS server using openssl or PowerShell
Align TLS registry settings between tiers
Update ARR proxy SSL flags

503.2.title: 503.2 - Concurrent request limit exceeded
503.2.description: siteLimits maxConnections or dynamicIdleThreshold policies rejected additional connections.
503.2.serverAdminConcern: High — Tune IIS site limits vs capacity.
503.2.applicationSupportConcern: Medium — Traffic spike or slow requests holding slots.
likelyCauses: Too low connection limits on busy sites
Slow upstream causing connections to linger
checks: Raise limits deliberately after measuring resources
Optimize slow endpoints
Scale out with ARR load balancing

503.3.title: 503.3 - ASP.NET Queue full
503.3.description: Requests exceeded the ASP.NET queue depth before worker threads became available.
503.3.serverAdminConcern: High — Thread pool and queue configuration.
likelyCauses: High latency SQL calls on many threads
checks: Profile slow queries
Convert to async
Increase servers or tune machine.config gingerly

503.4.title: 503.4 - FastCGI queue full
503.4.description: FastCGI processes could not dequeue requests quickly enough.
503.4.applicationSupportConcern: Medium — PHP or FastCGI app too slow.
checks: Raise instanceMaxRequests and concurrency settings responsibly
Optimize FastCGI workload
Add caching
